title: Who's Who: Astrid Bell
summary: Experimental mathematician whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Astrid Bell (1758–1821) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a experimental mathematician whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Bell devised the concordance scale in 1792, allowing laboratories to compare the residuals of objects thought to share a form. She insisted that a number without an uncertainty was only an opinion in respectable clothing.
The Bell tables remain standard references, although some values were revised after aperture experiments became possible.

For Alderwick readers, Astrid Bell is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
